# local 0010: sdld: a PC-relative byte after another byte with a relocation on the same T line gets a displacement that is 2 too low

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: In relr3, add 2 to rtofst after each byte relocation with R_BYT3. The change was not built or tested.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176, the file below links to `60 FE 20 00 F9`. The `jb` is at address 2 and has three bytes,
so the displacement from address 5 to address 0 is `FB`. With `F9` the instruction jumps to
0xFFFE.

```
        .area   CODE1 (ABS)
        .org    0x0000
        jz      0x0000
        jb      0x00,0x0000
```

It was assembled with `sdas8051 -l -o pcr.asm` and linked with `sdld -nf pcr.lk`. The command file
`pcr.lk` has the lines `-muwx`, `-i pcr.ihx`, `-M`, `pcr.rel`, an empty line, and `-e`.

The assembler writes both instructions to one T line. Each branch target is a field of three
bytes, of which the linker outputs one.

    T 00 00 00 60 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 00
    R 00 00 00 02 F1 07 04 00 00 F1 07 09 00 00

With a label on a line of its own between the two instructions, `sdas8051` begins a new T line
for the `jb`, and the file links to `60 FE 20 00 FB`, which is correct. The `jz`, which is the
first relocation of its line, is correct in both files.

The defect needs a relative branch for which the assembler writes a relocation. `mchpcr` in
`sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` resolves a branch to a label in the current area without one, so the
target has to be an absolute address, a label in another area, or an external symbol. For
`sdas8051`, a label after a later `.org` of an absolute area is in another area. Only the absolute
address was run with a relocation in front of the branch. The 2772 object files of the mcs51
libraries, built from r17176 with the patches of this report, have no PC-relative byte relocation.

## Cause

This was read in the source and not confirmed in a debugger. `relr3` in `sdas/linksrc/lkrloc3.c`
takes `pc + (rtp - rtofst)` as the address of the field that it relocates. `rtofst` is the number
of bytes in front of the field in the T line that are not output. It starts at `a_bytes`, and
`relr3` adds to it after a J11 or J19 relocation, after a pdk relocation, and after a byte
relocation with `R3_BYTX`. `sdas8051` writes each byte that has a relocation in the form with
`R_BYT3`, which is the `F1` in the R line above. `adb_24_lo` and the other `adb_24_` functions
clear `rtflg[]` for two of the three bytes, and `relr3` adds nothing to `rtofst` for them. For
each such relocation in front of a field, the address of the field is 2 too high, and a
PC-relative displacement is 2 too low.

`relr3` uses `rtofst` in three more places, which were not run: the page checks for the J11 and
J19 relocations of `ACALL` and `AJMP`, and the offset in its error messages. r14093, which set
the version for the 4.3.0 release, has the same lines.

## Related

The test case of bug #3703 has the two instructions of the file above in front of its `ACALL`.
With the patch for that ticket the file links, and its `JB` is `20 00 F9`.
